sections.title: 1. All-India Federation & Division of Powers (with Diarchy at Centre)

masteryZone.q: Which of the following was a constituent unit of the proposed All-India Federation under the 1935 Act?
opts: Provinces only
Princely States only
Both British Indian Provinces and Princely States
Presidency towns only
masteryZone.sol: The All-India Federation was proposed to comprise both British Indian Provinces and Princely States as units.

masteryZone.q: Identify the lists into which legislative powers were divided under the 1935 Act: (Select all that apply)
opts: Federal List
Provincial List
Concurrent List
Imperial List
masteryZone.sol: Powers were divided into three lists: Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent. There was no 'Imperial List'.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The proposed All-India Federation under the 1935 Act came into operation in 1937.
masteryZone.sol: The federation never came into operation because the princely states chose not to join it.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: The residuary legislative powers under the Government of India Act, 1935, were vested in the ______.
masteryZone.sol: The correct answer is Governor-General (or Governor-General of India).

masteryZone.q: Match the legislative lists with their respective count of items under the 1935 Act:
masteryZone.sol: Federal List had 59 items, Provincial List had 54 items, and Concurrent List had 36 items.

masteryZone.q: Which key subject of national interest was categorized under the Federal List of 59 items?
masteryZone.sol: External Affairs (or Defence, Currency, Census).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Diarchy at the Centre was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935.
Reason (R): The Act sought to divide federal subjects into Reserved and Transferred categories.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true, and the reason explains what diarchy at the Centre meant under the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed Federation of 1935:
Statement I: Accession to the federation was compulsory for British Indian provinces.
Statement II: Accession was entirely voluntary for the Princely States.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Provinces had no choice but to join the federation, whereas princely states could choose to join or remain outside.

masteryZone.q: Why were the princely states given the option to access the All-India Federation voluntarily rather than being forced to join?
masteryZone.sol: The princely states were semi-sovereign entities under British paramountcy governed by treaties and sanads, unlike British Indian provinces which were directly ruled by British administrators.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1935 Act handle conflicts between federal laws and provincial laws in the concurrent sphere?
masteryZone.sol: In the concurrent sphere, if a provincial law conflicted with a federal law, the federal law prevailed unless the provincial law had been reserved for and received the assent of the Governor-General.

masteryZone.q: A new technology emerged in 1938 that was not listed in the Federal, Provincial, or Concurrent lists. Explain how a law regulating this technology would be passed under the 1935 Act.
masteryZone.sol: The regulation would depend on the Governor-General. Under the 1935 Act, residuary legislative powers were vested in the Governor-General, who had the sole discretion to decide whether the Federal or Provincial legislature should enact the law.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of central diarchy as envisioned in the Government of India Act, 1935.
masteryZone.sol: Central diarchy divided federal subjects into Reserved and Transferred categories. Reserved subjects (Defence, External Affairs, Ecclesiastical affairs, Tribal areas) were administered solely by the Governor-General with his appointed counsellors. Transferred subjects were administered on the advice of ministers responsible to the Federal Legislature, introducing a dual executive structure at the center.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following acts abolished diarchy in the provinces?
opts: Indian Councils Act, 1909
Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1935
Indian Independence Act, 1947
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act of 1935 abolished diarchy in the provinces, introducing provincial autonomy instead.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following provinces were given a bicameral legislature under the 1935 Act? (Select all that apply)
opts: Bengal
Bombay
Punjab
United Provinces
masteryZone.sol: Bengal, Bombay, and United Provinces were bicameral. Punjab had a unicameral legislature.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Provincial Autonomy meant that the Governor was bound by the advice of the ministers in all circumstances.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Governor possessed discretionary powers and special responsibilities where he could act without or against ministerial advice.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: Under the 1935 Act, the Upper House in the provinces was called the ______.
masteryZone.sol: The Upper House was the Legislative Council, and the Lower House was the Legislative Assembly.

masteryZone.q: Match the provincial executive's actions with their respective requirements under the 1935 Act:

options.text: Governor acts completely on his own without consulting ministers
Governor consults ministers but is not bound by their advice
Governor must act in accordance with the cabinet's decisions

masteryZone.sol: Discretionary powers required no consultation; individual judgment involved consultation but no binding effect; ministerial advice was the standard autonomous track.

masteryZone.q: What was the total number of British Indian provinces that existed when the 1935 Act was implemented?
masteryZone.sol: 11 provinces.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Provincial Autonomy was short-lived, effectively ceasing by late 1939.
Reason (R): The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India's unilateral inclusion in World War II.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939 explains the collapse and suspension of provincial autonomy.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding provincial legislatures under the 1935 Act:
Statement I: The Legislative Assembly of a province had a fixed term of five years unless dissolved earlier.
Statement II: The Legislative Council of a province was a permanent body not subject to dissolution.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. The Lower House had a 5-year term, whereas the Upper House was a permanent body with rotating membership.

masteryZone.q: Why did nationalist leaders criticize the Governor's 'special responsibilities' under the 1935 Act?
masteryZone.sol: The 'special responsibilities' allowed the Governor to override elected ministers on key matters like public peace, minority rights, and civil services, making provincial autonomy hollow in practice.

masteryZone.q: How was the provincial cabinet appointed under the Government of India Act, 1935?
masteryZone.sol: The Governor appointed the ministers, who had to be members of the provincial legislature, typically selecting leaders who could command a majority in the assembly.

masteryZone.q: In 1938, the provincial assembly of Madras passes a bill to reform land revenue. The Governor believes it threatens the financial stability of the province. Analyze the Governor's options under the 1935 Act.
masteryZone.sol: The Governor could refuse assent to the bill, return it to the legislature for reconsideration with amendments, reserve it for the consideration of the Governor-General, or veto it entirely under his discretionary safeguards.

masteryZone.q: Define and explain the core principle of 'Provincial Autonomy' introduced in 1935.
masteryZone.sol: Provincial Autonomy meant the provinces were freed from central control and diarchical divisions. They became independent constitutional units, administering subjects in the Provincial List through an elected council of ministers responsible to a provincial legislature, representing a step toward self-governance.

sections.title: 3. Federal Court, Reserve Bank of India, and Institutional Safeguards

masteryZone.q: In which year was the Federal Court of India established under the 1935 Act?
masteryZone.sol: The Federal Court of India was established in Delhi in 1937.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following commissions were authorized under the Government of India Act, 1935? (Select all that apply)
opts: Federal Public Service Commission
Provincial Public Service Commission
Joint Public Service Commission
Imperial Civil Service Board
masteryZone.sol: The Act authorized Federal, Provincial, and Joint Public Service Commissions. No 'Imperial Civil Service Board' was created.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The 1935 Act completely separated the administration of Burma from India.
masteryZone.sol: Burma was separated from British India in 1937 under the provisions of the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: The 1935 Act extended separate electorates to depressed classes, labor, and ______.
masteryZone.sol: The correct answer is women. The electorates were extended to depressed classes (scheduled castes), women, and labor.

masteryZone.q: Match the institution with its primary function or characteristic under the 1935 Act:

options.text: Control currency and credit of the country

masteryZone.sol: RBI controlled currency; the Federal Court had multi-fold jurisdiction; and the Federal PSC managed civil service recruitments.

masteryZone.q: Who was appointed as the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of India in 1937?
masteryZone.sol: Sir Maurice Gwyer.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Federal Court of India was not the ultimate judicial body for British India.
Reason (R): Appeals from the Federal Court could be carried to the Privy Council in London.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. The Federal Court was subordinate to the Privy Council in London, which acted as the highest court of appeal.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding administrative units post-1935:
Statement I: Burma was separated from India and placed under a separate administration.
Statement II: Two new provinces, Sind and Orissa, were created.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements represent correct geopolitical reorganizations enacted under the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Reserve Bank of India established under the 1935 Act?
masteryZone.sol: It was established to unify and centralize the control of currency and credit in India, removing it from direct political influence and aligning with federal monetary management.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1935 Act reform the recruitment and management of civil services?
masteryZone.sol: It established the Federal Public Service Commission and Provincial Public Service Commissions, replacing patronage with organized recruitment examinations, though the Secretary of State retained control over key covenant services (ICS).

masteryZone.q: A dispute arises between the province of Bombay and the central federation regarding the distribution of customs revenue in 1938. Explain where and how this dispute would be resolved.
masteryZone.sol: The dispute would be brought before the Federal Court of India. Under its original jurisdiction, the Federal Court had the authority to resolve disputes between the federation and any of its constituent provinces.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of the Federal Court established under the 1935 Act as a precursor to the modern Supreme Court.
masteryZone.sol: The Federal Court of India (1937) was the first central constitutional court of the country. It had original jurisdiction in disputes between provinces/federation, appellate jurisdiction over High Courts on constitutional matters, and advisory jurisdiction to the Governor-General, laying the direct structural and procedural blueprint for the Supreme Court of India established in 1950.
